evals.name: python-library-flask
evals.prompt: I just inherited maintenance on the Flask repo checked out at /tmp/repos/flask (use the workspace bash tool to reach it). Generate a CLAUDE.md at the repo root plus whatever supporting docs make sense so that Claude actually knows its way around this codebase instead of re-exploring it every session.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md under 150 lines with overview/tech stack/structure/commands/additional-docs index, plus .claude/docs/architectural_patterns.md and at least one of testing_strategy.md / build_and_deploy.md. Commands must match pyproject.toml and CI. file:line references, no pasted code blocks of source.
assertions: CLAUDE.md exists at the repo root and is under 150 lines
Supporting deep-dive docs are placed under .claude/docs/
CLAUDE.md has an 'Additional Documentation' style index that lists every doc file created
Each index entry says WHEN to read the doc, not merely what it contains
CLAUDE.md contains no source-code snippets (fenced blocks, if any, are shell commands only)
Build/test/lint commands in CLAUDE.md all exist in the project's manifest, task runner, or CI config
A narrow single-file/single-test run command is given, not only the full suite
Deep-dive docs anchor claims with file:line references instead of pasted code
No code-formatting or style guidance (indentation, quotes, line length, import ordering, naming case)
architectural_patterns.md (or equivalent) exists and each documented pattern cites at least 2 distinct files
A project purpose/WHY section explains what the project is for, beyond restating the tech stack
Directory listing explains the purpose of each top-level directory rather than naming it
No data_model.md is invented for a project with no persistence layer
